original_question: For all sufficiently large n, is the n-vertex planar 3-uniform hypergraph with maximum spectral radius uniquely the one whose shadow graph is K_2 joined with P_{n-2}?
target_in_paper: Section 3, Conjecture 6 of arXiv:2305.10290, which restates the Ellingham–Lu–Wang conjecture on planar 3-uniform hypergraphs.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the main mathematical content of the target conjecture: the asymptotic quantifier ('for all sufficiently large n'), the object class (n-vertex planar 3-uniform hypergraphs), the extremal parameter (maximum spectral radius), the uniqueness claim, and the proposed extremal shadow graph K_2 ∨ P_{n-2}. That is essentially the substance of §3, Conjecture 6.
missing_details: The paper’s notion of a planar 3-uniform hypergraph should be stated explicitly: a 3-uniform hypergraph H is planar if its shadow ∂(H) has a planar embedding in which every hyperedge of H is the vertex set of a triangular face.
The shadow graph needs to be defined: V(∂(H)) = V(H), and uv is an edge of ∂(H) exactly when {u,v} is contained in some hyperedge of H.

The spectral radius here is the tensor/hypergraph spectral radius, not the adjacency-matrix spectral radius of an ordinary graph. For a 3-uniform hypergraph H on n vertices, the paper uses λ(H) = 3! max{∑_{e∈E(H)} ∏_{i∈e} x_i : x ∈ ℝ^n, ∥x∥_3 = 1}. This also makes clear that the ambient field is ℝ.
The extremal object is more precisely described in the cited source as the unique maximal hypergraph whose shadow is K_2 ∨ P_{n-2}; your draft omits this maximal-under-inclusion qualifier.
The phrase 'for all sufficiently large n' should be made stand-alone as: there exists n_0 such that the statement holds for every n ≥ n_0.

The join notation should be made explicit for stand-alone readability: K_2 ∨ P_{n-2} is the graph obtained from the disjoint union K_2 ∪ P_{n-2} by adding all possible edges between the K_2-part and the path.
refined_question: Does there exist an integer n_0 such that for every n ≥ n_0, among all planar 3-uniform hypergraphs H on n vertices—where the shadow ∂(H) is the graph with V(∂(H)) = V(H) and uv ∈ E(∂(H)) iff {u,v} ⊆ e for some e ∈ E(H), 'planar' means that ∂(H) has a planar embedding in which every hyperedge of H is the vertex set of a triangular face, and λ(H) = 3! max{∑_{e∈E(H)} ∏_{i∈e} x_i : x ∈ ℝ^n, ∥x∥_3 = 1}—the maximum spectral radius is attained uniquely by the planar 3-uniform hypergraph that is maximal under inclusion and whose shadow is the join K_2 ∨ P_{n-2}?
justification: The draft is already very close to the intended conjecture. The nearest official formulation inside arXiv:2305.10290 is §3, Conjecture 6. The sentences immediately preceding that conjecture provide the missing definitions of shadow, 3-uniform planarity, and hypergraph spectral radius. To make the question fully stand-alone and closer to the underlying Ellingham–Lu–Wang source that Conjecture 6 is summarizing, I made explicit the maximal-under-inclusion qualifier on the extremal hypergraph, since that qualifier is present in the source formulation and helps specify the conjectured extremal object sharply.
